ai_policy.summary: Springer Nature permits literature support, basic analysis and partial drafting under human oversight, verification and disclosure. Its framework permits interpretive and evaluative AI assistance with caution and human accountability; the FAQ separately says not to use AI to interpret data, so that tension must be observed.

disclosure.instructions: Describe research uses in Methods; add an AI Use Declaration at the end addressing manuscript preparation and accountability. Describe tool versions, dates, prompts and extent of use.
disclosure.section: AI authorship guidance; How can authors use AIGC?

restrictions: No AI authorship or delegation of scholarly judgment; no entire AI-written manuscripts, fabricated results or citations; protect confidential information.
Framework permits supervised interpretive support, but FAQ says AI should not interpret data; seek journal clarification for interpretive use.

policy_sources.note: Springer journal submission page identifies journal and publisher.

policy_sources.applicability: Springer Nature guidance applies to publisher journals, subject to journal-specific rules
policy_sources.note: Publisher guidance explicitly permits research, basic analysis, and partial drafting with conditions.

findings.issue: The publisher framework permits supervised interpretive assistance while its FAQ says not to use AI to interpret data; a blanket prohibition misstates the framework and leaves a policy tension.
findings.resolution: Preserve compatible status for permitted research, basic analysis and partial drafting, while stating both clauses and the need to clarify interpretive use.

notes: Reviewed all 18 candidate IDs against the other role files. Independently checked Sage policy, Springer AI guidance and current publisher metrics; Sage drafting ambiguity and Cambridge disclosure-only evidence remain unclear. Fee eligibility and geography assertions were challenged against cited evidence, and uncertainty retained where direct proof was incomplete. This is agent evidence review, not human scientific review.
2024 Organizational Research Methods figure is historical; newer official figure was not established. No acceptance-rate inference or difficulty rating is made.
